The held-out set is the same on every life (`heldout_sha256` adc7d902…, 24 texts), so the instrument is device-stable.

   - PR-x/B KL ratio over nights 1-15 spans 0.75-1.09 on s320 and 0.54-1.00 on s321. At n1 it is 0.87 and 1.00.
   - On s319, PR-x ran on W CPU and spans 0.77-1.28.
   - Method effects are in these ratios. Even so, no fp16 life comes anywhere near K-P's per-night ratios of 0.11-0.57.
   - The pooled K-P/B ratio is 0.118 at n15. The worst per-seed K-P/B ratio over nights 1-15 is 0.52 (s319), 0.42 (s320) and 0.57 (s321).
   - Removing even an implausibly large fp16 effect of -35% on KL, which is PR-x's best single-night ratio, leaves K-P/B at about 0.18 pooled at n15. That is still far under the 0.5 bar.

3. **The effect is on the trajectory, not a constant offset.** K-P KL grows from 0.07-0.09 at n1 to 0.29-0.35 at n15, about 3.5-5x. B grows from 0.13-0.18 to 2.4-2.9, about 14-23x. A systematic fp16 bias would be roughly a fixed scale or shift, not a divergence in growth rate. Night 1 is only 0.40-0.57 of B, so most of the gap opens during sleep, not at the start.

4. **The same-device replication reproduces the effect.** On CPU fp32 for both arms, one K-P night from B's drifted n15 home gives these held-out KL values:

| seed | B n16 | K-P n16 | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|

NLL drops from about 4.5-4.6 to about 2.7. This repeats on s316 (0.86 vs 2.80). It is one night from a drifted home, not a 15-night accumulation, so it supports direction and size but not the exact 0.118. s320 was still running when the note was written.
